Chapter Two: Entering the Royal Orbit—Service, Marriage, and the First Glimpses of Power.
Imagine stepping from a quiet family home straight into the glittering, unpredictable world of the royal court. That’s exactly what Katherine faced—a world where every move could be watched, and every word might echo farther than you’d expect. For her, joining the court wasn’t just an honor. It was a real test. Katherine’s first job? She became a lady-in-waiting. Now, this might sound glamorous, but it meant long days, endless tasks, and a constant balancing act. She’d tend to noblewomen, keep up with complicated court etiquette, and quietly navigate the tangled web of rivalries that always seemed to bubble just beneath the surface. Still, if you were smart and ambitious, the court was full of possibilities. Katherine paid close attention, seeing how influence could come not just from old family names or vast fortunes, but from loyalty, sharp instincts, and knowing when to speak—or when to stay silent. It was during these early years at court that Katherine met Hugh Swynford, a knight with a respectable, if not remarkable, reputation. Their marriage wasn’t about love stories or grand romance. Like many unions back then, it was practical—his land brought her security, and her royal connections gave him a bit of prestige. Together, they built a life that was stable, even if it didn’t make headlines. But Katherine never really left the world of the court behind. She kept serving, quietly building friendships and alliances that might one day open doors. Running a household, managing servants, and raising children taught her things she’d lean on later—practical skills that could make all the difference. And she saw, up close, just how quickly a noble family’s fortunes could rise or fall. One moment you’re in favor, the next, you’re out. Then, everything changed. Hugh Swynford died, and suddenly Katherine was on her own, with children to care for and her future wide open—but uncertain. In those days, being a widow meant you could easily slip into the background, lose your place in society. But Katherine? She didn’t shrink away. She weighed her options, drew on her resourcefulness, and decided to step forward instead. As Katherine navigated this new chapter, her life intersected with John of Gaunt—the formidable Duke of Lancaster and the king’s own son. At first, their connection was all about duty; Katherine was trusted to look after John’s children when his wife passed away. Yet, as they worked side by side, something deeper began to grow, quietly challenging the boundaries of what was considered proper. It was the beginning of a bond that would not only change their lives, but would ripple through English history itself.
